reasons.claim: If EBITDA normalizes to expected 2023 levels and is valued at a 10x multiple, the company would be worth 140 billion, a potential 5x.
reasons.quote: if things get to normal stability that's potential 5x

data_check.gap_note: he says 10, as-of 13.66 (2022-06-28); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: ebitda

reasons.claim: The company carries roughly 60 billion in debt against a 35 billion market cap, creating real uncertainty and risk.
reasons.quote: 60 billion of debt which creates high uncertainty which makes this also risky

data_check.gap_note: he says 6e+10, as-of 1.5098e+10 (FY2021); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: market cap

reasons.claim: AT&T dividend investors are dumping the stock irrationally simply because it does not pay a dividend, creating a value opportunity.
reasons.quote: it as a dividend it doesn't pay a dividend they are dividend investors and you have so much selling pressure that 50 down is not an issue

reasons.claim: Management plans to use robust free cash flow to pay down debt from 5x to 2.5x leverage, improving the investment case over time.
reasons.quote: they will use the free cash flow to reduce debt and lower it from 5x now to 3x and then stabilize it to 2.5 to free to keep the investment great

data_check.gap_note: he says 5, as-of 1.5098e+10 (FY2021); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: debt to ebitda target

reasons.claim: If debt reduction and growth plans falter the stock could stay flat or fall a further 20-40 percent, so the risk is real.
reasons.quote: it can always get ugly from an investment perspective and stay where it is or even go 20 30 40 percent lower and then be ugly

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: further downside

external_facts_used: AT&T shareholders received 71% of the new company in the spin-off
expected synergies of 3 billion per year to be reinvested into content

comparison to the Chemours spin-off from DuPont

critic.notes: ok — he calls it a spin-off buy with positive risk/reward and would allot 3% in a 30-position portfolio, though he personally passes for better opportunities; borderline fair_hold.
